- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or mixed (especially after recent spikes), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative and historical mean is falling — model tends to ignore downward momentum.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves in history — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects sharply.  
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum in forecasts when sentiment is weakly negative or neutral.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is consistently negative over last 5–7 days.  
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days of forecast window, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for delayed correction.
